en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Twelfth Chapter
Discussion on Karma:
Is all karma accompanied by its result? Yes.
Are all volitions accompanied by result?
One should not say so … [as before] … Are all volitions accompanied by result?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is volition that is indeterminate as fruition (vipākābyākatā cetanā) accompanied by fruition (savipākā)?
[The respondent replies: “It should not be stated thus…” [and so on].
Is all volition accompanied by ripening? Yes.
Is functional-indeterminate volition accompanied by ripening? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is all volition accompanied by result? Yes.
Is volition belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*) that is resultant and indeterminate (*vipākābyākatā*) accompanied by ripening (*savipāka*)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is all volition accompanied by ripening?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Then should it not be said that volition belonging to the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, and the unconditioned (apariyāpanna), which is karmically indeterminate as fruition, possesses fruition?
It should not be so stated… [and so on]…
Is every volition accompanied by fruition? Yes.
Is volition that is functional or indeterminate in the sense-sphere accompanied by fruition? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is all volition accompanied by result? Yes.

Are the volitions that are functional-indeterminate (kiriyā-byākatā) belonging to the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) and the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara) accompanied by karmic fruition (savipāka)?
One should not say so… [as before]… Are the volitions that are fruition-indeterminate (vipāka-byākatā) devoid of karmic fruition (avipāka)?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If resultant indeterminate volition is without result, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘All volition has a result.’”
Is volition that is functionally indeterminate (kiriyābyākatā cetanā) without fruition (avipāka)? Yes.
If volition that is functionally indeterminate is without fruition, then indeed you should not say:
“All volitions have a result.

[Is it then the case that] volitions belonging to the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, and the unincluded [sphere], as well as resultant and neutral volitions, are without a result?
Yes.
If volition that is not included [within the mundane], which is resultant-indeterminate, is without result, then indeed it should not be said:
"All volition has a result.
Is volition that is functional-indeterminate in the sense-sphere, the fine-material sphere, or the immaterial sphere without result?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If it is the case that volition which is functional and indeterminate in the formless realm is without result, then surely you should not say:
‘All volition has a result.’”
Is it not to be said that "all karma has a result"?
Yes, it is.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Bhikkhus, I do not say that there is an end to intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated without its being experienced; and that [experience] is either in this very life, or upon rebirth, or in some subsequent period”?
Does such a sutta exist?
“Yes.
“In that case, all karma has a result.
The Discussion of Karma is finished.
